narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 71.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your third-year class ranking had the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. You placed in the second decile, noticeably lower than the average of about 5.8 among students who were accepted. This academic performance in later years signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Next in importance was your undergraduate GPA of 3.0, which is modestly below the 3.23 average of accepted students. This feature worked in your favor by slightly lowering the predicted risk of failure, but its positive effect was not large enough to offset other factors.

Your family income bracket of upper-middle class ranked third. This characteristic also increased the chance of failure according to the model, though the effect was smaller than your class ranking.

Taken together, these elements led the system to conclude that the likelihood of passing the bar on the first try was too low for admission. 

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic record if you retake courses or pursue a post-baccalaureate program, and consider additional bar-preparation resources that have helped students with similar profiles succeed. Reapply once you can demonstrate clearer evidence of readiness. (248 words)

Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission.
